The story

A courier dies inside the Observatory Palace of House Baird. He carries a CHOAM offer on Arrakis, a sealed Bene Gesserit letter addressed to Zora Vey, and the mark of a rival House pressed into his palm. Before the morning is over, Christopher Baird learns why his father is frightened.

Married quietly before dawn, Christopher and Zora leave Aurelia for the Mentat academy. On the way they take on a sealed mathematics compact with the Spacing Guild and a CHOAM factor’s parting warning: “The Harkonnens already know your name.” At the academy, the great schools are about to teach side by side for the first time, and thirty students will graduate together or not at all.

See the pattern beneath the pattern.

    The Sisterhood invites Zora Vey for evaluation and gives no reason. What the letter leaves out matters more than what it says.

    Read Chapter Two

    Aboard the Heighliner, the Guild hands Christopher and Zora two sealed problems and keeps a third wafer dark. Its classification is BLACK VECTOR.

    Read Chapter Six

  • The cohort

    Thirty candidates, ten domains of critique, one question after every lesson, and a graduation condition they all share.

    Read Chapter Sixteen

The book’s ideas about evidence, memory and restraint became the starting point for two research preprints. They are kept apart from the story: the novel is fiction, and the papers are where those ideas are tested.

House Baird

Aurelia

  • Lord Christopher Baird

    Heir of House Baird of Aurelia. A strategist raised in an unusual cognitive tradition, poised between Mentat discipline, Ginaz ambition, old-Terra initiatic study, and the political future of his House.

    First named in the Prologue

  • Zora Vey

    Christopher’s lifelong companion, analytical equal, and secret wife. Raised beside him on Aurelia, even-tempered under pressure, with a hidden origin capable of destroying more than reputations if revealed.

    Christopher’s father and head of House Baird. Strategist, keeper of family secrets, architect of the House’s cautious expansion toward Arrakis.

    Christopher’s mother. Guardian of Aurelia while her husband moves among Imperial interests. Her family preserves traditions older than many Houses dare admit.

House Baird of Aurelia

“House Baird did not build Aurelia around wealth. It built around attention.”

Aurelia’s cities are quiet by Imperial standards: wide courtyards, shaded colonnades, observatories, libraries and academies. Violet mountains rise beyond the central continent, and silver inland seas carry the light through long evenings. Beneath the Observatory Palace lies the Deep Archive, which holds texts attributed to ancient Terra.

Family rule
Proceed as if every connection is provisional.

Rules for leaving home

  • Observe before acting.
  • Ask who benefits.
  • Do not confuse secrecy with safety.
  • Do not confuse access with status.
  • Never let Christopher pack unsupervised.

Recited at the landing field in Chapter Five. The last one is Zora’s.

Zora’s originSpoils Chapter One

The official story is simple: an orphan Lord Baird encountered on his travels near Ginaz, taken in and educated beside the heir. In Chapter One he tells them the truth. The Bene Tleilax, influenced by forbidden Ixian ideas, altered a naturally born child at the edge between biological intelligence and concepts inherited from thinking-machine architecture. A Bene Gesserit Sister escaped with the infant. Parts of Zora’s inheritance were selected from old Mentat lines, and one name survived in the correspondence under a private code: Elveris.

The forbidden machine survived too. It is hidden on Aurelia, passed through Zora’s line.

Field rules and old signals

“Bright eyes.”“Dim mouth.”

Their oldest field rule. Observe. Do not overshare.

The wrist signals come from a brittle leaflet in Aurelia’s archive, attributed without proof to an ancestor whose service once crossed the Atreides line. It describes pressure signals, breathing cues, eye movements and small gestures for when speech is unsafe. As children, Christopher and Zora turned it into a game.

The childhood set

  • Danger
  • Listen
  • Lie detected
  • Leave
  • Agree
  • Do not react

The Integrated Human Disciplines Program

THE INTEGRATED HUMAN DISCIPLINES PROGRAM

Provisional Charter — Landsraad Educational Compact

First Cohort

For the first time in known Imperial history, a cohort of Mentat students is trained across the great human disciplines in one program. A Bene Gesserit teaches beside Mentats, and Guild mathematicians, Suk physicians and Ginaz Swordmasters share their foundations. A select Landsraad committee folded the act into an Imperial indulgence package. Duke Leto Atreides did not write it; he built the coalition that made it possible.

Degrees

  1. BaccalaureateBroad fundamental competence across the integrated disciplines.
  2. MasterAdvanced specialization and application.
  3. Doctor of Human SynthesisOriginal work, defended before representatives of multiple schools, judged to contain new knowledge rather than competent repetition.

Ten domains of critique

Each domain is scored to ten, which means demonstrated mastery at the program’s standard, not perfection. No candidate entered at ten. Zora placed nine in analytical critique to Christopher’s eight; his weakest domain was biological. The schools shown are those the cohort portrait pairs with each domain.

  • AnalyticalMentat OrderMemory, logic, inference, strategy
  • MathematicalSpacing GuildNavigation, systems, the unseen
  • PoliticalLandsraadGovernance, economics, power, institutions
  • HumanisticHistory, philosophy, language, culture
  • EthicalTruth, duty, justice, faith, consequences
  • IntegrativeSynthesis across domains
  • Self-critiqueBias, identity, blind spots, continuous growth
  • SomaticBene GesseritPerception, discipline, human understanding
  • MartialGinazMovement, tactics, the human instrument
  • BiologicalSuk SchoolLife, medicine, human limits

Ordo Atreides

The Order of Atreides is the program’s special honor, for those who complete the full doctoral program, reach ten in every domain, and satisfy the participating faculties. Its page bears a scholarly hawk. In the book’s words, it was “named not because Duke Leto had demanded the honor, but because his sponsorship had made the experiment politically possible—and because he had refused to name it for himself.”

The confidentiality rule

  • If asked, tell the truth.
  • Do not fabricate cover stories.
  • Do not imply conspiracy.
  • Do not disclose restricted exercises, private consultations, or institutional material one was not authorized to share.
  • Answer the question actually asked.
  • Neither add nor subtract falsehood.

“What’s next?”

At the end of every lesson, examination, practicum, seminar or exercise, a candidate asks the instructor one question. Students never decide for themselves when a subject is finished. “Do not ask what score you received,” Registrar Cendes tells them. “Ask what is next.”

InstructionDemonstration“What’s next?”RepeatAdvanceIntegrateCertify

Sometimes the answer is “Nothing.” Reverend Mother Anirul calls that consolidation, not failure. Graduation comes when the participating faculties agree that no fundamental instruction remains that has to happen there.

The First-Cohort Principle

One fails, all fail.

Candidates may advance at different speeds and enter with different gifts, but the terminal condition is shared: if one candidate is not certified, the cohort fails. A struggling student stops being an embarrassment, and a gifted one can no longer profit from another’s weakness. “Then thirty minds confront the problem instead of one.”

Guiding distinctions

  • Truth is not certainty.
  • Uncertainty is not evidence that Truth does not exist.
  • Intuition is a signal, not a verdict.
  • Feeling is data, not automatically truth.
  • Access is not protection.
  • Potential is not mastery.
  • No one graduates alone.

Updating

On the way to breakfast after their first somatic lesson, Christopher and Zora adapt a tapping round from their training at home. At each point they hold one word internally, Updating. It gives the model permission to change; it does not order a feeling to disappear. If anxiety remains, that is the data.

The points

  1. Eyebrow
  2. Side of eye
  3. Under eye
  4. Under nose
  5. Chin
  6. Collarbone
  7. Under arm
  8. Crown

The loop

  1. Notice
  2. Tap
  3. Updating
  4. Breathe
  5. Reassess
  6. Name what changed
  7. Continue

“Intuition gets the first word.” “Truth gets the last.”

BLACK VECTOR

A sealed reciprocal research compact, struck aboard the Guild Heighliner with Factor Meret Sool and Ilyan Vohr. House Baird contributes work before it asks for privilege.

Wafer one

Problem A — Cenva Stability Problem

Given a family of admissible trajectories through continuously perturbed geometry, identify a criterion distinguishing a merely locally optimal path from one whose admissibility remains stable under bounded perturbations.

Wafer two

Problem B — Junction Allocation Problem

Given a Heighliner route network with uncertain loading times, political priority classes, finite hold allocation, and missed-connection penalties, construct a policy minimizing expected system-wide delay without revealing privileged route information to any client.

Third wafer

Inactive.

“Later.”

Status
Sealed reciprocal research compact between selected Spacing Guild representatives and Christopher Baird / Zora Vey as House Baird mathematical correspondents.
Terms
Mutual confidentiality. Provenance preserved. No publication without consent. No reverse engineering of privileged Guild systems. Dangerous discoveries may be frozen rather than exploited.
Deadline
“Until you have something useful.”
Potential reward
An invitation to Junction as Visiting Mathematical Correspondents, with restricted research access.

Open threads

Where things stand when Book I closes.

Show the open threadsSpoils all of Book I

  • The Arrakis concession

    CHOAM proposes a narrow Baird stake in spice operations under the existing Harkonnen administration. Lord Baird negotiates while Lady Baird holds Aurelia steady. Factor Cassian Vale gives Christopher a credential plate for Factor Lysa Ordan on Arrakis, and a warning that the Harkonnens already know his name.

  • The Sisterhood’s letter

    Zora is invited for evaluation at a time and place still to be named. No reason is given, and her possible Bene Gesserit training is undecided.

  • The dead courier

    A CHOAM cylinder, a Bene Gesserit letter and House Neral’s mark on one body. Staged, or meant to look staged. Who arranged it is still unknown.

  • The abstract

    A paper describing navigation as constrained branch selection, attributed to House Baird, reached the Guild through a private technical channel. Neither Christopher nor Zora knowingly sent it.

  • The fold

    During foldspace both field watches logged the same brief change in pulse, respiration and autonomic pattern. Compatible with Christopher’s model. Not confirming it.

  • The third wafer

    Still dark. When Christopher asked whether it concerned Norma, no one answered.

  • The machine on Aurelia

    Kept by Lord Baird under conditions designed to prevent anyone else from understanding it first.

  • Ginaz

    Christopher’s path after Mentat training. Swordmaster Torren has, by Christopher’s reading, already decided how long he would survive.

About

Fanfaire

Fanfaire is a home for fan-made worlds: campaign novelizations, fan fiction and the art that grows around them, presented with the care of a finished book.

The Quiet Calculus is the first work on its shelf.

Two research preprints grew out of it. They are separate, non-fiction works, described on the research page.

Author’s note

This is a fan-created campaign novelization inspired by Frank Herbert’s Dune universe and the Dune: Adventures in the Imperium roleplaying setting. House Baird, Aurelia, Zora Vey, the First Cohort, BLACK VECTOR, and the campaign-specific institutions and events in this volume are original to this campaign. Dune and its established setting, Houses, institutions, and characters belong to their respective rights holders. This work is intended as a noncommercial creative campaign artifact.

The story below reshapes the events of play into continuous literary prose. Dialogue and scenes are edited for flow, continuity, and readability while preserving the choices, discoveries, relationships, and themes established during the campaign.
